solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Channel head left light entertainment programme (8,4)

blocks.note: port = the left side of a ship
to light on something = to land on it
the bill = the list of acts in a show

annotation.surface: A TV channel boss has quit the light entertainment schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channel head' reads as a television executive, but the Channel is the English Channel and a head is a headland. Portland Bill is the rocky tip of the Isle of Portland on the Dorset coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Portland Bill is a headland jutting into the English Channel.

entries.clue: Stress [having] the narrowest of leads (5,2)

blocks.note: a phrasal verb meaning to emphasise or highlight
the smallest possible margin on a scoreboard: a single scoring unit ahead

annotation.surface: Under pressure because the lead in the match is razor-thin.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is the scoreboard reading: a side that is a point up leads by the smallest margin there is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for emphasise, plus the literal scoreline of a side ahead by the minimum.

entries.clue: Pound taken from account replaced by current statement (14)

indicatorNotes.taken from: the pound sign L is removed from the account word
indicatorNotes.replaced by: its place is filled by the word for current

blocks.note: a relation = an account or narrative, as in the relation of events
L = pound sterling, as in the £ sign

annotation.surface: A bank statement shows a pound debited and a current account credited.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is pure banking, with 'account' and 'current' as a bank account, but current here means present-day. Swap the L in RELATION for PRESENT and RE-PRESENT-ATION appears.
annotation.definitionFit: A representation is a formal statement of a case, as in making representations to a council.

entries.clue: Member I criticise for work as parliamentarian (9)

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

annotation.surface: An MP admits to attacking a colleague's record in the chamber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' tempts as a Member of Parliament, which suits the surface, but it is a limb.
annotation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which is a parliamentarian's work.

entries.clue: Woman with habit takes ecstasy instead of upping painkiller (7)

indicatorNotes.takes: the nun takes the other letters inside her
indicatorNotes.upping: in a down clue, sending letters up reads them backwards

blocks.note: for = instead of, as in 'substitute this for that'

annotation.surface: A nun gives up her painkillers and turns to ecstasy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instead of' looks like a swap instruction, but it only supplies a word, which 'upping' then turns round along with the ecstasy. Nurofen is a UK brand of ibuprofen.
annotation.definitionFit: Nurofen is a brand of ibuprofen sold as a painkiller.

entries.clue: Broadcast by Adele held up on secure line (7)

indicatorNotes.Broadcast: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered

annotation.surface: A radio station plays an Adele song that was delayed by a faulty connection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and Adele set up radio, and 'held up' looks like delayed, but a climber is belayed when held on a rope anchored to something fixed.
annotation.definitionFit: A belayed climber is held up by a rope made fast to a secure point.

entries.clue: Kosher joint of lamb maybe just the thing (5)

blocks.note: a leg is one joint of lamb among others
'it' = exactly the thing wanted, as in 'that's it'

annotation.surface: A butcher recommends a kosher cut of lamb as ideal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kosher' reads as a food law beside the lamb, but it is used in its slang sense of genuine or above board.
annotation.definitionFit: Legit and kosher are both slang for legitimate or above board.

entries.clue: Doctor who flew over a mile received guard on landing (5,9)

annotation.definition: Doctor who flew over a mile

blocks.note: a bannister is the rail guarding a stair landing

annotation.surface: A doctor flies a long way, gets a message, and meets an escort when the plane lands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flew' and 'landing' paint an aircraft, but the doctor ran: neurologist Roger Bannister was the first to run a mile in under four minutes, in 1954.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Roger Bannister, a doctor, famously sped over a mile in under four minutes.

entries.clue: Dusty tray quiet old man fills again when empty (3,3)

indicatorNotes.fills: the SH and PA go inside the other word, filling it
indicatorNotes.when empty: an emptied word keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: AGAIN with its middle removed leaves A…N

annotation.surface: An old man silently refills a dusty tray whenever it runs out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Again when empty' reads as refilling the tray, but it strips a word to its outside letters. An ash pan is the tray under a fire grate that catches the ash.
annotation.definitionFit: An ash pan is the tray beneath a grate that collects the ash, so it is dusty by design.

entries.clue: Popular gorge full of litter (2,3)

blocks.note: to pig = to eat greedily, to gorge

annotation.surface: A well-known ravine has become strewn with rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a ravine and 'litter' like rubbish, but litter here is a brood of piglets: a sow that is in pig is pregnant.
annotation.definitionFit: A sow in pig is pregnant, carrying a litter.

entries.clue: Practising engineers keen to sue when titanium’s not used (9)

indicatorNotes.when titanium’s not used: the symbol for titanium, TI, is removed

blocks.note: litigious = eager to go to law
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium; LITIGIOUS loses it to become LIGIOUS

annotation.surface: Working engineers are eager to take legal action unless titanium is left out of the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Practising' looks like a verb about training engineers, but it is the adjective for someone who actively follows a faith.
annotation.definitionFit: Practising describes an active follower of a faith, the everyday sense of religious.

entries.clue: New self-test laboratory’s closing, being responsible for infections (6,3)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters are made into something new
indicatorNotes.closing: the closing letter of the word

annotation.surface: A lab that sold a new home-testing kit is shutting down, and it is to blame for spreading infections.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb, but it is a noun here: a living creature.
annotation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly is a creature that spreads sleeping sickness.

entries.clue: Player I should have said sorry to’s head twisted (5)

indicatorNotes.head: the head of 'to' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.twisted: the whole string is turned round

blocks.note: a PS (postscript) adds what the writer should have said

annotation.surface: A remorseful note about an actor whom the writer failed to apologise to.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a guilty confession, but it is three pieces: a postscript, a puzzled 'sorry?' and a T, read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A thesp, short for thespian, is an actor, a player on the stage.

entries.clue: Beard on Patrick’s face ginger yet dark (7)

indicatorNotes.face: a word's face is its front, its first letter

blocks.note: the awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or wheat

annotation.surface: Patrick's ginger beard somehow looks dark on his face.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beard' is placed 'on' P and RED, so it comes after them in an across answer. The awn is a botanical beard, not a facial one.
annotation.definitionFit: The predawn hours come before sunrise, while it is still dark.

entries.clue: Spooner’s broken racket in this? (7)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: bust = broken; it takes the D sound from the next word
din = racket, a loud noise; it takes the B sound from the word before

annotation.surface: A smashed tennis racket belongs in the rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racket' tempts as a tennis racket that has broken, which is where the bin comes in, but it is a din, a noise. A dustbin is British for a rubbish bin.
annotation.definitionFit: A broken racket would be thrown in the dustbin.

entries.clue: Alarming figure conflated soccer with war (9)

indicatorNotes.conflated: two words fused into one mixed mass

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; 'with' joins the two words

annotation.surface: A worrying statistic treats football as if it were warfare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alarming figure' suggests a scary number, but the figure is a shape in a field that alarms birds.
annotation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a figure meant to alarm crows.

entries.clue: What she has put on card fades (7)

indicatorNotes.put on: in an across answer, one word placed on another follows it

blocks.note: a card is a joker, a wit

annotation.surface: Whatever she writes on her greeting card soon fades.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a greeting card, but it is old slang for an amusing person, a joker.
annotation.definitionFit: Fades and withers share the sense of losing freshness and colour, as cut flowers do.

entries.clue: The reason to admit one’s singular fantasy? (6)

indicatorNotes.to admit: the outer word lets the others in

annotation.surface: A dreamer asks why he should admit his one peculiar fantasy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks possessive, but it is read as 'one is', so I (one) plus 'M ('s = is) gives I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: Whimsy is playful fantasy or fanciful notion.

entries.clue: Federal agents infiltrating assigned section (7)

indicatorNotes.infiltrating: the agents get inside the other word

blocks.note: set = assigned, as in set homework

annotation.surface: FBI agents have infiltrated the unit they were given.
annotation.walkthrough: G-men is US slang for FBI agents, 'government men'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: one slice of an orange can be called either word.

entries.clue: Plastic can isn’t made of tin (7)

indicatorNotes.Plastic: plastic = mouldable, so the letters are reshaped

annotation.surface: A plastic can is, naturally, not made of tin.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a true statement about containers; 'Plastic' is the instruction, not the material. Stannic comes from stannum, Latin for tin.
annotation.definitionFit: From stannum, Latin for tin: the chemists' adjective for tin compounds.

entries.clue: Odd bits of timber after sinking initially keep one man alive (5,2)

annotation.type: charade + container + first letter + alternate letters

indicatorNotes.initially: the first letter of the word
indicatorNotes.keep: the timber letters hold ONE inside

annotation.surface: Floating bits of wood keep a man alive after his ship goes down.
annotation.walkthrough: The survival story is a decoy: 'man alive' is not a rescue but an exclamation of surprise, and 'keep' puts the survivor inside the timber letters.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Stone me!' and 'man alive!' are both British exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: Blind cat has penetrated airport’s controlled area (7)

indicatorNotes.has penetrated: the cat has got inside the other word

blocks.note: to blind = to swear, as in effing and blinding; to cuss
a tom is a male cat

annotation.surface: A blind cat has slipped into the restricted zone at an airport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blind' looks like an adjective for the cat, but it is a verb: to blind is British slang for to swear, from 'effing and blinding'.
annotation.definitionFit: Customs is the controlled area where an airport checks arriving goods.

entries.clue: Word during service that must be repeated back (5)

indicatorNotes.back: the service word is read backwards

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the war'
in tennis a let is a serve that must be played again

annotation.surface: A word spoken during a church service has to be repeated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests church, but it is a tennis serve. 'Word' here means information, as in 'send word'.
annotation.definitionFit: Word in the sense of news, as in 'send word', matches the slang for gathered information.

entries.clue: Raised border mainly contains plant with colourful flowers (5)

indicatorNotes.mainly: most of the word: its last letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.contains: the border word holds the other inside

blocks.note: LINE, a border, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A gardener's raised bed is mostly given over to a bright flowering plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised border' reads as a garden bed, which suits the plant, but 'raised' is UP and 'border' is LINE.
annotation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of colourful flowers.

entries.clue: Shopping sounded more revolting every second for hikers (9)

indicatorNotes.sounded: spoken, so the word's sound is used

blocks.note: grosser = more revolting; GROCER is said the same way
every second letter of hIkErS; 'for' is the link

annotation.surface: Hikers find the supplies they carried grow more disgusting by the second.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Every second' suggests a time scale, but it picks out alternate letters of 'hikers'.
annotation.definitionFit: Groceries are the shopping you bring home from the supermarket.

entries.clue: Pressure that is in loo breaks pump, perhaps display model (9)

indicatorNotes.is in: pressure and 'that is' go inside the loo
indicatorNotes.breaks: the loo splits the shoe open and sits inside

blocks.note: a pump is a kind of shoe

annotation.surface: Water pressure in the toilet has broken the pump, so now it is just for show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pump' looks like plumbing beside the loo, but a pump is a light dancing shoe; loo is British for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A showpiece is a model put on display as the finest example.

entries.clue: Mature Trollope somewhat like earlier works (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only part of the phrase is used

annotation.surface: Anthony Trollope's later novels resemble his early ones.
annotation.walkthrough: The novelist Trollope is only there to supply letters across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: Retro means imitating the style of earlier times or works.

entries.clue: Doctor drew iron shot, putting it straighter (2,5,5)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it

annotation.surface: A golfer's doctor pulled an iron shot while trying to hit it straight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person and 'drew' like a golf shape, but doctor is the verb and the definition is a phrase introducing a plainer version.
annotation.definitionFit: 'In other words' introduces a restatement put more plainly.
